blogs.title: Goodbye Tokens, Hello Patches: How BLT Makes AI Smarter and Faster
blogs.description: An introduction to the Byte Latent Transformer (BLT), explaining how it replaces rigid tokenization with dynamic 'patches.' This post breaks down how the model intelligently groups raw bytes based on complexity—spending more computing power on unpredictable parts of text and skipping ahead through easy patterns—to achieve state-of-the-art performance while cutting inference costs by up to 50%.

blogs.title: Why Your AI Stumbles Over Typos (And How Raw Bytes Fix It)
blogs.description: Explore the hidden weaknesses of current Large Language Models when faced with messy input, strange formatting, or rare languages. This article dives into BLT's ability to process raw bytes directly, demonstrating why this approach makes models significantly more robust to noise, better at understanding phonetics, and superior at handling low-resource languages compared to traditional token-based systems.

blogs.title: The New Scaling Law: Why Growing Patches Beats Growing Vocabulary
blogs.description: A deep dive into the economics of AI training. We analyze BLT's groundbreaking finding that you can simultaneously increase model size and patch size within a fixed compute budget. Learn why this 'dynamic allocation' strategy allows byte-level models to eventually outscale traditional tokenizers, offering a new roadmap for building massive, efficient AI without the bottlenecks of fixed vocabularies.
